LESSON: INTRODUCTION TO SALTS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Physical Chemistry
Topic 2.2: Introduction to Salts
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 30

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Introduction to Salts, part of Physical Chemistry in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: How do salts behave when exposed to air? 2. How can salts be prepared in the laboratory?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Introduction to Salts together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: The learner brainstorms and carries out activities with peers to establish the

meaning of salt

● Learning to learn: The learner develops relationships by sharing what they have learnt while carrying out

experiments to prepare salts

● Creativity and imagination: The learner makes observations as they carry out experiments to determine solubility of

salts in water.

Values:
● Respect: The learner appreciates the opinion of others as they carry out activities to categorise salts as soluble or

insoluble

● Unity: the learner cooperates with peers as they discuss the applications of salts

36

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (waste management): The learner appropriately disposes of laboratory

waste after preparing different salts

● Life skills (Self-esteem): The learner confidently makes presentations in plenary on the findings about the effects of

excessive use of salts on environmental sustainability

Suggested learning resources

Tactile braille label, large print labels, digital devices with assistive technology, reagents, volume measuring apparatus

with tactile stops, print and braille reference materials.

Suggested Key Skill(s)

• Prepare salts using different methods in the laboratory.

• Describe behaviours of salts when exposed to the air.

• Describe applications of salts in day to day life.
